question: Two increment cores from the same tree give different ring counts. Analyse biological and sampling causes.
modelAnswer: Check whether either core missed the pith, false or missing rings, decay, coring height and ring interpretation; cross-date and reconcile the cores.

question: A ring-width series shows an abrupt narrow period followed by recovery. Analyse plausible causes and evidence needed.
modelAnswer: Consider drought, competition, damage or management release; compare neighbouring trees, climate and stand-history evidence before attribution.

question: Whorl count and increment-core age disagree for a conifer. Analyse the assumptions behind each estimate.
modelAnswer: Whorls may be missing, multiple or obscured, while a core may miss pith and needs a height-age correction; verify both methods.

question: Current annual increment rises while mean annual increment is still lower. Analyse the stand's growth stage.
modelAnswer: MAI continues rising while CAI exceeds it; culmination occurs when CAI and MAI meet, so the stand has not yet reached maximum MAI.

question: Repeated DBH measurements imply implausibly negative growth. Analyse the field records.
modelAnswer: Check tree identity, measurement height, tape tension, bark condition, units, transcription and damage; retain justified biological change only after verification.

question: Evaluate estimating the age of a broadleaved tree solely from whorl count.
modelAnswer: Reject the method because annual whorls are not reliably expressed; use increment cores, stem analysis or documented planting age as appropriate.

question: Evaluate accepting one off-centre increment core without a pith correction as total tree age.
modelAnswer: The estimate is biased low unless missing radius/rings and years to coring height are estimated and uncertainty is reported.

question: Evaluate projecting the most recent five-year volume increment unchanged for the next 30 years.
modelAnswer: Growth changes with age, competition and disturbance; use an appropriate growth model or scenarios and report uncertainty.

question: Design an increment-coring protocol for estimating tree age.
modelAnswer: Specify tree selection, coring height and direction, pith assessment, ring preparation/counting, height-age correction, duplicate checks and uncertainty.

question: Design a permanent-plot protocol for measuring diameter growth.
modelAnswer: Use durable tree IDs and measurement marks, fixed DBH convention, calibrated tools, repeat dates, data checks, mortality/recruitment records and increment calculations.

question: Design a cross-dating quality-control procedure for difficult ring series.
modelAnswer: Use multiple cores and trees, visual/statistical pattern matching, flag false or missing rings, document corrections and retain raw measurements.

question: Design a study to estimate the culmination of mean annual volume increment.
modelAnswer: Measure or model volume across ages, calculate CAI and MAI consistently, identify their intersection, quantify uncertainty and avoid extrapolation beyond data.

question: Design a method comparison between whorl count and increment coring in young conifers.
modelAnswer: Apply both methods to the same trees, establish a reference age where possible, include height-age corrections, calculate bias and explain failures.

question: Design an age-and-growth report suitable for a management decision.
modelAnswer: State objective, sample and methods, age corrections, growth period, CAI/MAI results, uncertainty, limitations and the management interpretation.
